rich_narrative.summary: The Muslim Foundation primary concerns center on financial reserve accumulation, weak governance oversight, and an 11% revenue contraction in FY2024. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="2">Total Revenue of $2,222,033</cite>, down from $2,504,911 in FY2023 [2]. The foundation holds <cite id="1">74.8 months of working capital in reserves</cite>, representing over six years of operating expenses held without a documented plan for deployment [1]. Furthermore, the organization holds a <cite id="1">Charity Navigator score of 64.0/100</cite> and meets zero out of 20 BBB Wise Giving Alliance standards [1]. On program delivery, the foundation allocates a <cite id="1">Program expense ratio of 72.4%</cite> toward operating its local mosque and educational programs [1]. While fundraising costs remain low at <cite id="1">$0.08 per $1 raised</cite>, the lack of outcome tracking and undisclosed board governance severely restrict organizational evaluation [1].
